Predis.ai vs VEXI: Templated AI Posts or Your Own Content?
Predis.ai generates templated reels, carousels and ads from a prompt. VEXI edits your own footage, makes long-form video, designs and posts.
Predis.ai generates posts and short videos from a prompt or a product link. Here is how it compares with one app built around your own footage and your own business.

Predis.ai generates reels, carousels, single images, video ads and captions from a prompt, a product link, an image or a template. It also tracks competitors' ads. Core is $19 a month with no auto-posting; Rise is $40 a month and adds auto-posting; Enterprise+ is $212 a month. Every plan starts with a 3-day trial.

VEXI (formerly Social Realtr) is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.

The difference is whose content it is. Predis.ai is quick at turning a prompt or a product page into templated posts. Its site describes no editing of the clips you shot and names only short video formats. VEXI starts from your own footage, photos and business: you ask, and the post comes back edited, designed, captioned and posted. VEXI costs more than Predis.ai: plans are $199, $399 or $599 a month. What you pay for is the work you no longer do.
Predis.ai starts from a prompt, a product link, an image or a template. Its site does not describe editing the videos you filmed.
Send VEXI the clips you shot and they come back cut, with B-roll, music and captions, sized for each platform.
Every video format its site names is short: reels, stories, shorts and video ads.
VEXI makes long-form videos on every plan, and turns a long recording into its best clips, captioned.
The $19 Core plan says "No Auto Posting". Auto-posting starts on Rise at $40 a month.
VEXI schedules and posts to your connected accounts itself.
Predis.ai is rated 4.4 on Trustpilot. Some reviewers report a charge before the trial ended and files locked once a subscription lapsed.
